div.head: II Cn 24
div.ab: ⁊ nan man nan þingc ne bigce ofer feower peniwurð, ne libbende ne licgende, butan man hæbbe getrywe gewitnesse feower manna, seo hit binnan byrig, sy hit upp on lande.
And nan man nan þincg ne bycge ofer feower penigweorð, ne libbende ne licgende, buton man hæbbe getreowe gewitnesse feower manna, sy hit binnan byrig, sy hit up on lande.
Et nemo aliquid emat supra IIII denariorum ualens, mobile uel inmobile, nisi habeat credibile testimonium IIII hominum, sit in ciuitate, sit extra.
⁊ nan man nan ðing ne bycge ofer feower peninga weorð, ne libbende ne licgende, buton mon habbe getreowe gewitnysse feower manna, sy hit binnan byrig, sy hit up on lande.
And nan man nan þingc ne bigce ofer feower peniwurð, ne libbende ne licgende, butan man hæbbe getrywe gewitnesse feower manna, seo hit binnan byrig, sy hit upp on lande.

Und niemand kaufe etwas über 4 Pfennigwerth (-ge Werth B), weder lebendes noch liegendes [todte Fahrhabe], ohne dass er Zeugenschaft von 4 glaubwürdigen Männern hat, sei das [Kaufen] in der Stadt oder auf dem Lande.
And let no one buy anything over four pennies' worth, either living or lying [dead chattels], unless he has the trustworthy witness of four men, whether it be in a borough or up in the country.

And no-one shall buy anything over four pence in value, either livestock or other property, unless he have four men as trustworthy witnesses, whether [the purchase be made] within a town or in the open country.
And no one is to buy anything worth more than fourpence, neither live-stock nor other goods, unless he has the trustworthy witness of four men, whether it is in the borough or in the country.
And no one shall buy anything worth more than four pence, either livestock or goods, unless he has four men as honest witnesses, whether he is in a town or in the country.
div.note: G's ‘peniwurð’ is so at a line end, perhaps forgetting ‘-ga’ at the start of the next line. Liebermann compares IV Eg 6.2.
